title: accounts/<id>.json
description: An account, open or closed. Its values are in the history files, which refer to it by ID. Lifecycle: open it by creating the file with opened; close it by setting closed (it leaves check-ins and today's totals, keeps its values, and still shows in every chart up to that day: nothing is deleted); reopen it by removing closed; rename or re-categorise it by editing the fields (the history refers to the ID, which never changes). Deleting the file, with its values, is only for mistakes.

id.description: The same as the file name.

name.description: Display name; change it whenever you like.

kind.description: What kind of account it is. The kind decides what the account records (ACCOUNTS.md): cash and savings accounts a balance with money in and out, savings also its interest; loan, mortgage and creditCard are debts, recorded as negative balances; brokerage, crypto and metals accounts record trades; the others a balance. belongings are things you own that lose value and might sell (a car, a bike, a boat). A taxPot is money set aside for a tax bill paid later: a balance with money in and out (out is the tax paid from it, in a refund) that counts in neither net worth nor plans by default, and what moves into it from your other accounts is tax (PROGRESS.md, "Savings rate"). It also sets the default of assetClasses, and how what a value saved is worked out (history-month.schema.json, saved).

currency.description: The currency of the account's balances and cash.

opened.description: The first day the account counts toward net worth.

closed.description: The last day it counts. Absent while the account is open. A closed account leaves check-ins and today's totals, keeps its values, and still shows in every chart up to that day.

valuation.description: How values are recorded. balance: one amount. trades: holdings, purchase cost and cash come from the account's trades (TRADES.md), and its valuations record only cash. Default: trades for brokerage, crypto and metals, balance for the other kinds.

assetClasses.description: The asset mix of values recorded as a single balance, for the breakdowns and the planner: a balance account's, or the balances in an investment account's imported history (positions follow their instruments). Default: cash for cash and savings, realEstate for property; otherwise such a value counts as other.

availableFromAge.description: The age from which plans can draw on the account, e.g. 67 for a pension fund. Until 1 January of the first year you're that age, plans keep it apart: locked, at its own mix, not wealth-taxed (PLANNER.md). Left out, it can be drawn at any age. The app suggests 65 for a new pension fund.

withdrawalTaxRate.description: The share of every amount taken from the account that goes to tax, from 0 to 1 (error planner.withdrawalTaxRate), set by hand like the plan's tax rates: such as "0.2" for money taxed as income when it comes out (a traditional 401(k) or IRA), or "0" for money that comes out tax-free (a Roth IRA). Plans check the range but don't use the rate yet: they tax the account like any other investment, as they do when it's left out.

includeIn.description: What the account counts in. Both default to true, and to false for a taxPot, whose money is owed; a primary home would normally set plan to false.

successor.description: The account that replaced this one, e.g. when you switched banks, so charts stay continuous.

depreciation.description: The share of its value a belongings account is estimated to lose a year, such as "0.15" for a car, above 0 and below 1; other kinds, and other values, ignore it. After each value, its value on a later day is estimated from it, compounding a year at a time, until the next value is typed; the next value trues it up. Left out, it keeps its value until then. Belongings' change in value is saved, so its loss of value is spent (PROGRESS.md, "Savings rate").

values.description: Where the account's values come from. imported: from imported files (statements, exports, spreadsheets). typed: also typed by hand, a balance on a date (source manual), with no money in and out. Default: imported. Only balance accounts take typed, of every kind but cash, creditCard and taxPot, whose money in and out keeps coming from their statements; those kinds, and accounts that record trades, read it as imported. An investment account set to typed is written with valuation balance. Typed savings or investments turn Trends off (ACCOUNTS.md). A starting estimate (tagged estimate) takes typed values until it's closed, whatever this says.
